questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Hungary?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Hungary article.

questions.proof: Budapest is the country's capital and largest city, and the dominant cultural and economic centre.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Hungary on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Hungary on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Budapest?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Hungary is Budapest.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Hungary about 93,011 square kilometres; Croatia about 56,594 square kilometres; Moldova about 33,844 square kilometres; Armenia about 29,743 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Hungary?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Hungary on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Hungary article.

questions.proof: It is bordered by Slovakia to the North, Ukraine to the Northeast, Romania to the East and southeast, Serbia to the South, Croatia and Slovenia to the Southwest, and Austria to the west.
